items.title: Pencil
items.summary: Traditional graphite, and the medium I'm most comfortable and fastest with. Pencil suits every portrait and every animal. If you're unsure, choose pencil.
items.intro: Traditional graphite, and the medium I'm most comfortable and fastest with. Pencil suits every portrait and every animal, from soft puppy fur to wiry terrier coats.
items.coverAlt: Detail of a pencil portrait of a schnauzer

items.title: Ink
items.summary: I paint the ink on with a brush, then add detail with ink pens, for a bolder, more graphic look. It takes a little longer, and occasionally a photo isn't suited to ink. I'll always let you know.
items.intro: I paint the ink on with a brush, then add detail with ink pens. The result is bolder and more graphic, with deep blacks and crisp whiskers.
items.coverAlt: Detail of an ink portrait of a pug

items.title: Colour Pencil
items.summary: Layer upon layer of coloured pencil, for rich, true-to-life fur, eyes and markings. It works best from a well-lit photo where your pet's real colours are clear.
items.intro: Layer upon layer of coloured pencil, for rich, true-to-life fur, eyes and markings. It works best from a well-lit photo where your pet's real colours are clear.
items.coverAlt: Detail of a colour pencil portrait of a chocolate spaniel
